newsitem.title: JAPAN: Aftershocks continue to rock southern Japan.
newsitem.headline: Aftershocks continue to rock southern Japan.

text.p: Minor tremors continued to rock Japan's southern island of Kyushu on Wednesday in what authorities say are aftershocks from a strong earthquake which hit the region the previous day.

A fairly strong aftershock, measuring 4.7 on the Richter scale, hit Kyushu island at 8.32 a.m. on Wednesday (2332 GMT Tuesday), but most of the tremors following Tuesday's quake were small, Japan's Meteorological Agency said.
As of 9.00 a.m. (0000 GMT), the agency reported 78 tremors since Tuesday afternoon, of which 40 could be felt.

There were no immediate reports of damage or injuries from the aftershocks. Authorities however warned local residents to take extra precautions as forecasts for heavy rain in the area could cause landslides and other damage.
On Tuesday, a strong earthquake measuring 6.2 on the Richter scale shook Kyushu island, causing minor damage and slightly injuring at least 34 people.
The epicentre of Tuesday's quake was near the town of Sendai in Kagoshima Prefecture in the southern part of the island. Sendai is about 985 km (615 miles) southwest of Tokyo.

Another earthquake, also registering 6.2 on the Richter scale, struck Sendai on March 26, and the area had been experiencing several minor aftershocks from the March tremor. The earlier earthquake caused no damage.
